item: A write-gate hold says where its seconds went: insert, savepoint, other statement, commit, between statements
summary: The gate keeps, for the hold in progress, the seconds its owner thread spent in INSERT statements, savepoint statements, any other statement and commits (listeners on the Engine class return at once for any other thread: +1 us a statement for them, +4.5 us for the holder, measured on SELECT 1); what no measured statement covers is between_statements. A hold of 30 s or more writes seconds_by into the storage-events journal as the watchdog's sample (a running statement counted so far) and exactly at its end. The member keeps the split on as many of the longest holds as the slot's free bytes allow (the budget is not raised): the shortest holds give it up first, each saying zip-budget, counted; with every name at the cut 6 of 20 keep it, with ordinary names all 20; a hold with none says not-recorded, never zeros. A session's commit is exact, a raw connection's an upper bound. 25 gate tests, 3 member tests, 10 mutants killed.
